newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Skandia says Lars-Eric Petersson new CEO.
newsitem.headline: Skandia says Lars-Eric Petersson new CEO.

text.p: Swedish insurance group Skandia said on Friday Lars-Eric Petersson had been appointed president and chief executive officer of the group, replacing Bjorn Wolrath who will remain a board member.
Petersson, 46, is currently head of Nordic operations, and will assume his new post on January 1, 1997, Skandia said in a statement.

"Lars-Eric Petersson, who has broad financial experience, has been employed by Skandia since March 1993, inter alia as head of international non-life insurance and reinsurance and head of Skandia's investment operations," it said.

Wolrath, whose outspoken views on Swedish fiscal policy led to a surge in Swedish bond yields in August 1994, will undertake "certain future-oriented projects" and will hold a number of external assignments, retaining a seat on the board.
Skandia said Wolrath had voiced a personal desire to step down from his position, which he has held for the past 16 years in addition to 10 years of service in other positions within the group.
The company has also appointed Jan Carendi as senior executive vice president of the Skandia group.
